theory.text: When you start using AI to build, there's a sneaky temptation: treat it like a self-driving car. You say "build me an app", it takes off, and you wait for the result like a passenger. Does it work? Rarely. And when it does, you've built something you know nothing about — which is like owning a house without holding the keys.
⚠️ The passenger trap. If the AI decides everything for you, you'll build things you can't even fix when they break. And they will break.

Here's the right mindset: you're the architect, the AI is the construction crew. You decide what to build, where the door goes, how many rooms. The crew executes, you check. You don't lay every brick yourself, but you're the one accountable for how the building stands.

bad.label: 🚧 Bricklayer
bad.content:
"How do I write this function?"
Thinks in lines of code
Executes the request
Gets lost in details

good.label: 🏛️ Architect
good.content:
"What problem am I solving?"
Thinks in outcomes and systems
Decides the request
Holds the big picture

theory.output:
Sure. First though — who'll use it, and for what?
  • Just visitor email, or also a message?
  • Should it reach you via email, or save to a database?
  • Want spam protection?

(The AI isn't wasting time. It's handing back the decisions only YOU can make.)

theory.text: 🔑 The golden rule: decide first, prompt second. If you don't know what you really want, no prompt in the world can read your mind.
If an LLM wrote every line of your code, but you've reviewed, tested, and understood it all, that's not vibe coding. That's using an LLM as a typing assistant.

exercise.prompt_template: When using AI to build software, my role is to be [BLANK], not the typist. I decide [BLANK], the AI executes.

blanks.hint_1: Think about who designs a building vs. who lays the bricks.
blanks.hint_2: It's the role that holds the vision and makes the big decisions.
blanks.explanation: The answer is 'the architect'. You hold the vision, the AI executes. It's the role shift that separates a vibe coder from a passenger.

blanks.hint_1: Which decision can ONLY you make before prompting?
blanks.hint_2: It's not about code. It's about the destination.
blanks.explanation: The answer is 'what to build' (or 'the outcome'). Defining the destination is your non-negotiable job. The AI can figure out how to get there, not where to go.

outro.recap: You learned the role shift: the AI executes, you decide. Without you at the helm, you'll build things you can't control.
outro.next_prompt: Next lesson: how to think in outcomes instead of steps (and why it works better).
